item.text:
**6B.9 Research Note**

**Bottom line:** Sisi in 2024 showed some real institution-building in social policy, but most of it was top-down, executive-led, or externally scaffolded. The strongest independent evidence still points to a system that remains personalized and security-dominated, so the record is at best mixed and probably negative on “durable beyond personal rule.”

**Accepted claims**
- **[Women's Empowerment Strategy 2030](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/strategies/womens-empowerment-strategy-2030/)** - State Information Service, 2024-03-12 - The presidency assigned the women’s strategy to the government, state agencies, and the National Council for Women as a working document with follow-up mechanisms. This is evidence of institutional packaging for gender policy, though it is still presidentially driven and not proof of autonomy. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.8
- **[President El-Sisi Meets Prime Minister and Members of the New Government](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-meets-prime-minister-and-members-of-the-new-government/)** - State Information Service, 2024-07-03 - Sisi told the new cabinet to strengthen institutional frameworks, coordination, integrity, transparency, and public communication. That is a direct pro-institution signal, but it is general governance language rather than proof of durable independent institutions. - **QIDs:** 6B.9
- **[President Sisi swears in new government ministers](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-sisi-swears-in-new-government-ministers/)** - State Information Service, 2024-07-03 - The reshuffle installed a broad cabinet with technocratic portfolios, including social solidarity, labor, health, education, planning, and finance. This supports some bureaucratic institutionalization around social policy, though it still does not show independence from the presidency. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.5, 6B.7
- **[Arab Republic of Egypt: Technical Assistance Report - Public Investment Management Assessment](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/technical-assistance-reports/issues/2024/04/02/arab-republic-of-egypt-technical-assistance-report-public-investment-management-assessment-547051)** - IMF, 2024-04-02 - The IMF said Egypt had already taken steps to improve infrastructure access and public investment management through new legislation, information systems, and staff-capacity efforts, with Education 2.0 and health infrastructure rollouts underway. This is meaningful institutionalization, but it is process evidence, not proof of institutions surviving beyond Sisi. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.5
- **[World Bank Group Statement of Support to Egypt’s Development and Reform Efforts](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2024/03/18/world-bank-group-statement-of-support-to-egypt-s-development-and-reform-efforts)** - World Bank Group, 2024-03-18 - The Bank framed the agenda around inclusive growth, human capital, resilience, and protecting the poorest, with health, education, and social protection systems as explicit priorities. This suggests a policy frame that outlives a single patron, but it is still a programmatic intent statement rather than proof of durable institutions. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.5
- **[House of Representatives approves drafted Social Solidarity bill](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/house-of-representatives-approves-drafted-social-solidarity-bill/)** - State Information Service, 2024-12-01 - The bill aimed to unify support programs, regulate grants, and formalize eligibility for Takaful and Karama. This is strong evidence of formalized welfare administration, and it is the clearest positive sign that some social policy was being institutionalized rather than handed out ad hoc. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.5
- **[Launch of the Joint UN Programme under the Joint Platform for Migrants and Refugees in Egypt](https://www.unhcr.org/eg/news/launch-joint-un-programme-under-joint-platform-migrants-and-refugees-egypt)** - UNHCR Egypt, 2024-09-30 - Egypt, the UN, and the EU launched a program to support health and education for refugees and migrants in vulnerable situations. This is a real institutional support signal, but it is also externally co-funded and narrowly targeted, so durability beyond Sisi is only partial. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.5

**Negative / limiting claims**
- **[Egypt: President al-Sisi must reject new asylum law which violates refugee rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/12/egypt-president-al-sisi-must-reject-new-asylum-law-which-violates-refugee-rights/)** - Amnesty International, 2024-12-03 - Amnesty said the new asylum law was rushed, lacked meaningful consultation, and shifted asylum responsibility to a permanent committee affiliated with the prime minister and ministries. That is formal institution-building on paper, but the criticism is that it is opaque, rights-weak, and not obviously durable or independent. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.7
- **[Egypt: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024)** - Freedom House, 2024 - Freedom House said Sisi and the security apparatus dominate policymaking, parliament lacks a meaningful check, and the anti-corruption body is controlled by Sisi. This is strong evidence against durable institutions surviving his personal control. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.7
- **[Egypt’s Al-Sisi Has Caged Himself In](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/26/egypts-al-sisi-has-caged-himself)** - Human Rights Watch, 2024-02-26 - HRW said Sisi relied on coercion and the military-security services, while dismantling independent institutions and avoiding party-based rule. This is direct contrary evidence to the claim that he was building autonomous institutions that could outlast him. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.8, 6B.7
- **[World Report 2024: Egypt](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/egypt)** - Human Rights Watch, 2024 - HRW said the national dialogue had not produced recognizable policy reforms, civic space remained heavily curtailed, and independent organizations faced judicial and security harassment. That undercuts any claim that durable, self-sustaining institutions were taking root. - **QIDs:** 6B.9, 6B.8

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong independent evidence that Sisi created social institutions that are clearly insulated from his personal control or likely to persist unchanged after him.
- The positive record is mostly executive-led policy design, official self-presentation, or externally supported programs.
- The strongest negative sources say the real governing structure still runs through Sisi, the security apparatus, and weakly independent oversight bodies, which makes durability uncertain at best.
